title: Celigo mcp-server
description:
Request body for creating or updating an MCP server. On PUT, include the
full `connections`, `tools`, `apis`, `prompts`, `resources`,
`permissionSets`, and `policies` arrays because omitted arrays are
cleared; `upstreamMcpConnections` and `_networkPolicyId` are the
exceptions and keep their stored value when omitted. Every array entry
must be an object — a `null` entry in `tools`, `apis`, `prompts`,
`resources`, or `upstreamMcpConnections` is rejected with 422
`mcp_server_invalid_array_item`. Use PATCH to update individual fields
without affecting these arrays.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
MCP servers expose Celigo tools, builder-mode APIs,
and inline prompt templates as MCP-compatible endpoints for consumption by AI
agents and MCP clients.

x-celigo-canon.reason: Do not require apis, description, disabled, or oauth on write — a minimal name-plus-relativeURI create succeeds and the server defaults the rest (empty description, disabled true, empty arrays, no oauth). Universal stored presence is server-defaulted/UI-written.

name.description: Display name for the MCP server.
x-celigo-ai-guidance: Displayed in the UI to identify the server's purpose.

x-celigo-canon.reason: Server requires a non-empty name on create and caps its length, but accepts an empty name on update; the spec requires a non-empty name on every write.

relativeURI.description:
URI path segment for the MCP server endpoint. Must be unique per account —
duplicates are rejected with 422 `mcp_server_duplicate_relative_uri`. Only letters,
numbers, dashes, and underscores after the leading slash (the server's error message
also claims colons and dots are allowed, but they are rejected in practice). Creation
also requires the account to have an account alias set (422
`mcp_server_account_alias_required` otherwise).
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Set the field to a unique pathname per account that starts with a forward slash
followed by a single path segment containing only alphanumeric characters,
underscores, and hyphens.

If not provided,
a `url` field can be supplied instead and the pathname will be extracted automatically.

description.description: Description of the MCP server's purpose.
x-celigo-ai-guidance: Optional description of the MCP server's purpose and capabilities.
examples: Exposes customer management tools for AI agent consumption

x-celigo-canon.reason: The server's size limit is measured in bytes at two per character, so the character cap is half the model's declared size; one character over is rejected.

disabled.description:
When true, the server refuses MCP clients. New servers start disabled.
Enabling requires at least one enabled tool, API, resource, or prompt,
or one enabled and available upstream capability — otherwise the write
is rejected with 422 `mcp_server_enablement_requires_enabled_item`.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Enable the items first, then the server: a PUT or PATCH that sets
disabled to false while every item is disabled fails with 422
"mcp_server_enablement_requires_enabled_item".

connections.description:
Connections the server's tools run through, each flagged for whether
end users must supply their own credentials. Always returned — an
empty array when none is listed — and cleared when omitted on PUT.
Together with `tools[].overrides.connections[]` this is the set
`GET /v1/mcpservers/{_id}/connections` reports.

items.description:
One connection the server's tools use, with the flag that decides whether
each end user must supply their own credentials for it. Connections named
here and in `tools[].overrides.connections[]` together form the set that
`GET /v1/mcpservers/{_id}/connections` lists.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Reference a live connection owned by this account: an unknown id fails
with 422 "resource_not_found" and the same connection listed twice with
422 "resource_invalid".

_connectionId.description:
Connection a tool on this server runs through. Each connection can
appear once in the array, and only account-owned connections belong
here — an end user's `mcpChild` connection is not a valid reference
(`mcp_child_connection_usage_not_allowed`).

requiresEndUserCredentials.description:
When true, each end user must supply their own values for the fields
the connection's `endUserProvidedFields` names (through the MCP setup
page) before calling tools that use it; those values are stored as a
per-user `mcpChild` connection. The platform contract is that clearing
the flag, or dropping the connection from every server that set it,
invalidates the end users' `mcpChild` connections for it.

showInPublicRegistry.description:
When true, this enabled server is eligible for the public MCP
registry on accounts that have opted in. Defaults to `false`.
Cannot be set on a disabled server. Callers without publish
permission receive `403` on changes to this field; echoing the
unchanged value in a PUT does not `403`.

tools.description:
Tool entries referencing Celigo Tool resources. Duplicate `_toolId`
values are rejected. Names must be unique across both `tools` and `apis`.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Tool entries reference Celigo Tool resources;
each entry exposes a Tool as an MCP tool endpoint.

Duplicate `_toolId` references are not allowed,
and Tool names must be unique across all tools and APIs in the server.

items.description:
A tool entry that maps a Celigo Tool resource to an MCP tool endpoint.
The referenced tool's input schema must have `type: "object"`.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
A tool entry within an MCP server references a Tool resource;
tool names across all tools and APIs within the same MCP server must be unique
and follow the MCP naming convention (alphanumeric,
underscores, hyphens, dots only).

_toolId.description:
Tool resource ID. The referenced tool must exist and have an
input schema with `type: "object"`.
x-celigo-ai-guidance: Reference to the Tool resource that this MCP tool exposes.

name.description:
MCP tool name exposed to clients. Must be unique across all tools
and APIs within this server.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Must be unique across all tools and APIs within this MCP server.
Only alphanumeric characters, underscores, hyphens, and dots are allowed.
Maximum length: 128 characters (enforced by validation).

disabled.description: When true, this tool is disabled and will not be exposed to MCP clients.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Indicates whether this tool is disabled within the MCP server;
disabled tools are not exposed to MCP clients.
At least one tool, API, resource, or prompt must be enabled for the
server itself to be enabled.

annotations.description:
MCP-standard annotations that hint at the behavior of a tool.

These annotations follow the Model Context Protocol specification and help
AI agents and MCP clients understand how a tool behaves without executing it.
All fields are optional hints — they are not enforced by the server.

title.description:
Human-readable title for the tool, displayed in MCP client UIs.

If not provided, the tool's `name` field is used instead.

x-celigo-canon.reason: The server's size limit is measured in bytes at two per character, so the character cap is half the model's declared size; one character over is rejected.

destructiveHint.description:
Hints that the tool may perform destructive operations such as
deleting or permanently modifying data.

idempotentHint.description:
Hints that calling the tool multiple times with the same input
produces the same result without additional side effects.

openWorldHint.description:
Hints that the tool interacts with an open-world environment
(e.g., external APIs) where results may vary between calls.

readOnlyHint.description: Hints that the tool only reads data and does not modify any state.

overrides.description:
Per-server overrides for a tool's internal resources.

When a tool is added to an MCP server, its connections, exports, imports,
and routers can be customized for this specific server context without
modifying the underlying tool definition. This enables reusing the same
tool across multiple MCP servers with different configurations.

connections.description:
Connection overrides. Each entry maps an abstract connection reference
in the tool to a concrete connection resource for this server.

_abstractId.description:
The abstract connection identifier from the tool definition.
This is the connection reference that will be replaced.

_id.description: The concrete connection resource to use in place of the abstract reference.

x-celigo-canon.reason: Server accepts and stores _abstractId-only entries verbatim, and _borrowConcurrencyFromConnectionId is a documented alternative — uniform stored pairing is not a requirement.

_borrowConcurrencyFromConnectionId.description: Optional connection from which to borrow concurrency limits.

requiresEndUserCredentials.description:
When true, each end user must supply their own credentials for
this connection (a per-user `mcpChild` connection) before the
tool runs for them on this server. Same meaning as the
server-level `connections[].requiresEndUserCredentials`; by the
platform contract the connection counts as requiring end-user
credentials when either entry sets it. Only the MCP server
override shape carries this field — flow and API tool overrides
do not.

exports.description:
Export (lookup) overrides. Customize export resources used within the tool,
including connection bindings, scheduling, response mappings, and
adaptor-specific settings.

_abstractId.description: Abstract export identifier from the tool definition

_connectionId.description: Override the connection used by this export

x-enumDescriptions.webhook: Event-driven export triggered by incoming webhook calls.
x-enumDescriptions.distributed: Export distributed across multiple NetSuite worker nodes.
x-enumDescriptions.test: Export used for testing and validation only.
x-enumDescriptions.delta: Incremental export that fetches only records changed since the last run.
x-enumDescriptions.once: One-time export that runs a single time and does not repeat.
x-enumDescriptions.tranlinedelta: Transaction line-level delta export for NetSuite transaction lines.
x-enumDescriptions.simple: Basic export that fetches all matching records on each run.
x-enumDescriptions.blob: Binary large object export for file-based data.
x-enumDescriptions.all: Export that retrieves all records without filtering.

pageSize.description: Override the page size for pagination

skipRetries.description: When true, skips retries on failure.
x-celigo-ai-guidance: Whether to skip retries on failure

proceedOnFailure.description: When true, continues processing subsequent records after a failure.
x-celigo-ai-guidance: Whether to continue processing on failure

fields.description: Field-level mappings that copy individual values from the response back onto the record.

extract.description: Path in the response to extract the value from. Uses dot notation to navigate nested objects.

generate.description: Target field path on the record where the extracted value is stored.

lists.description: Array-level mappings for one-to-many data in the response.

generate.description: Target array field on the record where the mapped list items are stored.

fields.description: Field mappings applied to each item in the response array.

extract.description: Path within each response list item to extract the value from.

generate.description: Target field path within each mapped list item.

imports.description:
Import overrides. Customize import resources used within the tool,
including connection bindings, hooks, response mappings, and
adaptor-specific settings.

_abstractId.description: Abstract import identifier from the tool definition

_connectionId.description: Override the connection used by this import

proceedOnFailure.description: When true, continues processing subsequent records after a failure.
x-celigo-ai-guidance: Whether to continue processing on failure

fields.description: Field-level mappings that copy individual values from the response back onto the record.

extract.description: Path in the response to extract the value from. Uses dot notation to navigate nested objects.

generate.description: Target field path on the record where the extracted value is stored.

lists.description: Array-level mappings for one-to-many data in the response.

generate.description: Target array field on the record where the mapped list items are stored.

fields.description: Field mappings applied to each item in the response array.

extract.description: Path within each response list item to extract the value from.

generate.description: Target field path within each mapped list item.

preMap.description: Hook that runs on each page of records before the import's mappings are applied.

function.description: Function to invoke within the referenced script.

_scriptId.description: Script containing the hook function named in `function`.

postMap.description:
Hook that runs after the import's mappings are applied but before records
are sent to the destination system.

function.description: Function to invoke within the referenced script.

_scriptId.description: Script containing the hook function named in `function`.

routers.description:
Router overrides. Customize routing behavior for specific branches
within the tool, including branch filters and routing strategies.

_abstractId.description: Abstract router identifier from the tool definition

x-enumDescriptions.first_matching_branch: Routes each record to only the first branch whose criteria match.
x-enumDescriptions.all_matching_branches: Routes each record to every branch whose criteria match, creating copies.

x-enumDescriptions.input_filters: Evaluate routing criteria using declarative filter expressions.
x-enumDescriptions.script: Evaluate routing criteria using a custom JavaScript function.

_scriptId.description: Script containing the routing function named in `function`.

function.description: Function within the referenced script that returns the name of the branch to route to.

examples: Records routed to the North America region

x-enumDescriptions.1: Version 1 of the Celigo expression-based filter format.

rules.description:
Filter rules in Celigo expression-based filter format. Array-based DSL where
the first element is an operator (e.g. "equals", "and", "or"), followed by
operands which can be nested expressions.

apis.description:
API entries referencing Celigo builder-mode API resources. Only
builder-type APIs are supported. Names must be unique across both
`tools` and `apis`.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Each entry exposes an API as an MCP tool endpoint.
Duplicate `_apiId` references are not allowed.
Only builder-type APIs are supported.
Tool names must be unique across all tools and APIs in the server.

items.description:
An API entry that maps a Celigo builder-mode API resource to an MCP
tool endpoint. Script-type APIs are not supported.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Each API tool maps a Celigo API to an MCP-compatible tool endpoint;
only builder-type APIs (not script-type) can be used in MCP servers.

Tool names across all tools and APIs within the same MCP server must be unique
and follow the MCP naming convention:
alphanumeric characters, underscores, hyphens, and dots only.

name.description:
MCP tool name exposed to clients. Must be unique across all tools
and APIs within this server.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Must be unique across all tools and APIs within this MCP server.
Only alphanumeric characters, underscores, hyphens, and dots are allowed.
Maximum length: 128 characters (enforced by validation).

_apiId.description: API resource ID. Must reference a builder-type API (not script-type).

disabled.description: When true, this API tool is disabled and will not be exposed to MCP clients.
x-celigo-ai-guidance: Whether this API tool is disabled within the MCP server.

resources.description:
Files from Celigo Storage exposed to MCP clients as MCP resources.
Each entry references a storage file by `_fileId`; the same file can
appear only once. Always returned in responses — servers created
before resource support return an empty array. Not supported on
sandbox servers.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Each resource exposes a Celigo Storage file to MCP clients.
The referenced file must exist and belong to the same account,
and each _fileId may be used only once per server.
Omit the field entirely for sandbox servers — combining
resources with sandbox: true fails with 422.

items.description:
A resource entry that exposes a Celigo Storage file to MCP clients.
Clients discover resources via `resources/list` and fetch file content
via `resources/read`. Resources are not supported on sandbox servers —
setting `resources` together with `sandbox: true` returns 422
`mcp_server_resources_not_allowed_in_sandbox`.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Each resource entry references a file in Celigo Storage (a StorageItem);
the file must exist, be an active file (not a folder), and belong to the
same account — otherwise the create or update fails with 422
"mcp_server_file_not_found" on the offending "resources.N._fileId".

Do not set resources on a sandbox MCP server; the API rejects the
request with 422 "mcp_server_resources_not_allowed_in_sandbox".

_id.description:
Server-generated identifier for the resource — the grant handle
referenced as `resource:<_id>` in resource grants and in
`permissionSets[]._resourceIds`. Preserved across PUT by matching on
`_fileId`, so pointing an entry at a different file assigns a new
`_id` and breaks grants that reference the old one.

title.description:
Human-readable display title shown to MCP clients alongside the
file. Free text, unlike tool and API names (which are
regex-constrained MCP identifiers).

_fileId.description:
Celigo Storage file exposed by this resource. Must reference an
active file (not a folder) owned by the account — invalid references
return 422 `mcp_server_file_not_found`. Each file can be referenced
only once per server; duplicates return 422
`mcp_server_duplicate_file_not_allowed`. Manage files via
`GET /v1/storage/items`.

disabled.description:
When true, the resource is hidden from MCP clients and its file is
not served. Resources are disabled by default; set to false to
expose the file.

prompts.description:
Prompt templates exposed to MCP clients. Each prompt has a unique
`name` and may declare `arguments` that clients supply via
`prompts/get`.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Unlike `tools` and `apis` (which reference other Celigo resources by ID),
each prompt is defined inline on this server.
Prompt names have their own namespace — a prompt name may collide with a tool or API name,
but must be unique within `prompts[]`.

items.description:
A prompt template entry on an MCP server.

Prompts are inline, reusable templates that MCP-compatible clients (Claude,
Cursor, Celigo AI Agents, etc.) discover via `prompts/list` and fetch via
`prompts/get`. Each `{{placeholder}}` inside a message template becomes a
declared argument that the client supplies at invocation time; the
backend performs Handlebars substitution before returning the rendered
messages.

Unlike `tools[]` and `apis[]` — which reference other Celigo resources by
ID — a prompt is stored inline on the MCP server document. There is no
separate "Prompt" resource type.

`prompts/get` returns rendered messages of shape
`[{role, content: {type, text | data, mimeType?}}]` — `text` for `text`
content, or `data` (base64) + `mimeType` for `image`/`audio`. This schema
captures the stored template; the rendered output is not part of the
persisted document.

_id.description:
Server-generated identifier for the prompt — the grant handle
referenced as `prompt:<_id>` in end-user, group, and role resource
grants and in `permissionSets[]._promptIds` (older grants written as
`tool:<_id>` still validate but are not reported by effective
access). Identity is preserved across updates by matching on `name`,
so renaming a prompt assigns a new `_id` and breaks grants that
reference the old one.

name.description:
MCP prompt name exposed to clients via `prompts/list`.

Must be unique within `prompts[]` on this server. Only alphanumeric
characters, underscores, hyphens, and dots are allowed. Prompts have
their own namespace — a prompt named `summarize_meeting` does not
collide with a tool or API of the same name.

Maximum length: 128 characters. Duplicate names return 422
`mcp_server_duplicate_prompt_name`.

title.description:
Human-readable display title shown alongside `name` in MCP clients.

Unlike `name` (the MCP identifier, regex-constrained), `title` is
free text. Optional — clients fall back to `name` when omitted.

x-celigo-canon.reason: The server's size limit is measured in bytes at two per character, so the character cap is half the model's declared size; one character over is rejected.

description.description:
Optional description of what the prompt does. Shown to MCP clients
during discovery so users and LLMs can choose the right prompt.
examples: Summarize a meeting transcript into key decisions and action items.

x-celigo-canon.reason: The server's size limit is measured in bytes at two per character, so the character cap is half the model's declared size; one character over is rejected.

arguments.description:
Declared arguments for the prompt. Every `{{placeholder}}` referenced
in `messagesTemplate[*].template` should appear here so MCP clients
know what to supply when invoking the prompt.

items.description:
A single declared argument for a prompt. Argument names appear as
`{{name}}` placeholders inside `messagesTemplate[*].template` and are
substituted with client-supplied values at invocation time.

name.description:
Argument name. Must match `^\\w+$` (letters, digits, and underscores
only) so it can be referenced as a Handlebars `{{placeholder}}` in the
message template. Hyphens, dots, and other characters are not allowed
here (even though prompt `name` permits them) — they would break the
template parser.

description.description:
Optional human-readable description of the argument. Shown to MCP
clients during discovery; useful for guiding LLMs that supply values.

x-celigo-canon.reason: The server's size limit is measured in bytes at two per character, so the character cap is half the model's declared size; one character over is rejected.

required.description:
Whether the client must supply this argument. Defaults to `true`.
When `false`, the client may omit the argument and the
`{{placeholder}}` is left empty after substitution.

messagesTemplate.description:
Ordered list of message templates forming the prompt body. At least
one entry is required. Each entry renders to a single message after
Handlebars substitution.

items.description:
A single message entry inside a prompt's `messagesTemplate[]`. Renders to
a `{role, content: {type, text|data, mimeType?}}` object in the
`prompts/get` response after Handlebars substitution.

x-enumDescriptions.user: Message from the user or human participant.

role.description:
Message role exposed to MCP clients.

Only `user` and `assistant` are supported. `system` role messages are
not allowed at this layer — express system-level intent inside the
first user or assistant template.

contentType.description:
Type of content this message carries.

- `text` — `template` holds the Handlebars-templated text body.
- `image` / `audio` — `data` (base64) and `mimeType` are required
  (omitting `mimeType` returns 422 `mcp_server_prompt_mimetype_required`);
  `template` is not used.
- `resource` — reserved for future use; the authoring UI does not
  currently expose this option.

template.description:
Handlebars-templated text body. Use `{{argumentName}}` to reference
declared arguments — they are substituted server-side before the
message is returned to the client.

Up to 4 KB inline. Templates larger than 4 KB are automatically
offloaded to S3 (up to a 1 MB hard limit) and rehydrated on read.

Only relevant when `contentType` is `text` (the default).

data.description:
Base64-encoded binary content for image / audio messages. Only allowed
when `contentType` is `image` or `audio`.

Up to 10 MB via S3 offload.

mimeType.description:
MIME type for the binary `data`. Required when `contentType` is `image`
or `audio` (e.g. `image/png`, `audio/wav`).

x-celigo-canon.reason: The server's size limit is measured in bytes at two per character, so the character cap is half the model's declared size; one character over is rejected.

mockInput.description:
Sample argument values used to preview / test-run the prompt in the
authoring UI — a plain object mapping argument names to sample values
(e.g. `{"username": "John Doe"}`). Keys usually mirror `arguments[].name`
but this is not enforced. Has no effect on `prompts/get` rendering for
MCP clients.

disabled.description:
When true, the prompt is hidden from MCP clients — omitted from
`prompts/list` and not fetchable via `prompts/get`. New prompts
default to disabled; set to false to expose the prompt. An enabled
prompt also satisfies the server-level enablement rule on its own.
Prompts saved before this field existed are reported as
`disabled: false`.

permissionSets.description:
Named bundles of this server's tools and APIs — shown as "Capability
Sets" in the UI — granted to end users as a unit via `pset:<_id>`
capability strings. Omitting the field on PUT resets it to an empty
array, erasing every set and rewriting the grants that reference
them — always send the complete array back. Absent from responses for
servers not saved since permission sets were introduced (unlike
`resources`, the field is not normalized to an empty array).
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Not editable via PATCH (/permissionSets is not a whitelisted path).
To change permission sets safely, GET the server, modify
`permissionSets`, and PUT the complete document back with every
set's `_id` intact.

items.description:
A named bundle of this server's tools and APIs — shown as a "Capability
Set" in the integrator.io UI — granted to end users as one unit through
the `pset:<_id>` capability string on end-user, group, and role resource
grants. There is no standalone permission-set resource: sets live only
inside the MCP server document, and each set's `_id` is the stable handle
that grants reference.

Deleting a set — or resubmitting it without its `_id` — rewrites every
grant that references it: the `pset:` capability is replaced with the
set's constituent `tool:`, `api:`, `prompt:`, and `resource:`
capabilities at removal time.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
When updating a server via PUT, send the complete `permissionSets` array
and round-trip every existing set with its `_id` intact — an omitted set
is removed and the grants that referenced it are flattened to its
individual tool/API capabilities.

_id.description:
Server-generated identifier for the set — the grant handle referenced
as `pset:<_id>` in resource grants. Send it back unchanged on PUT to
preserve the set's identity; a set submitted without its `_id` is
treated as a brand-new set and assigned a fresh one.

name.description:
Display name for the set. Must be unique per server,
case-insensitively — duplicates are rejected with 422.

x-celigo-canon.reason: The server's size limit is measured in bytes at two per character, so the character cap is half the model's declared size; one character over is rejected.

description.description: Description of what the set grants and who it is for.
examples: Read-only invoice lookups for the finance team

x-celigo-canon.reason: The server's size limit is measured in bytes at two per character, so the character cap is half the model's declared size; one character over is rejected.

x-enumDescriptions.read: Read-level access, aligned with the `mcp:read` OAuth scope
x-enumDescriptions.write: Write-level access, aligned with the `mcp:write` OAuth scope

accessLevel.description: OAuth-aligned access level the set pins for everyone it is granted to.

_toolIds.description:
Tools included in the set. Every entry must be a tool already
attached to this server — a `tools[]._toolId` or an upstream tool
row `upstreamMcpConnections[].tools[]._id`. Any other id, including a
prompt `_id`, is rejected with 422 `resource_invalid`; prompts go in
`_promptIds`.

_apiIds.description:
Builder-mode API resources included in the set. Every entry must
reference an API already attached to this server through
`apis[]._apiId` — referencing one that is not attached is rejected
with 422 `resource_invalid`.

_promptIds.description:
Prompts included in the set, referenced by `prompts[]._id`. An id
that is not a prompt on this server is rejected with 422
`resource_invalid`. Absent from responses for sets saved before
prompt grants existed.

_resourceIds.description:
File resources included in the set, referenced by `resources[]._id`.
An id that is not a resource on this server is rejected with 422
`resource_invalid`. Absent from responses for sets saved before
resource grants existed.

upstreamMcpConnections.description:
Remote MCP servers proxied through this one, each attached via an
`mcp`-type connection with a whitelist of the upstream tools, prompts,
and resources to expose. Always returned — an empty array when none is
attached. Unlike every other array on the server, it is preserved
when omitted on PUT; send an empty array to detach everything.

items.description:
A remote MCP server proxied through this server. The `mcp`-type connection
holds the upstream endpoint and credentials; `tools`, `prompts`, and
`resources` whitelist which of its capabilities this server exposes, each
row joined to the upstream catalog by `upstreamName`. Discovery, run from
the integrator.io UI, fills the read-only catalog fields (`discoveryStatus`,
`lastDiscoveredAt`, and each row's `title`, `description`, `annotations`,
`discoveredAt`, `unavailable`). A write carries only `_connectionId`,
`alias`, and each row's `upstreamName`, `disabled`, `overrides`, and `uri` —
every other field is taken from the stored row, and a write that includes
`upstreamMcpConnections` re-approves the current upstream definitions
(`approvedDefinitionHash` is re-pinned and `changedSinceApproval` reset).
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Attach only connections of type "mcp" that belong to this account: any
other type fails with 422 "mcp_upstream_connection_invalid_type", an
unknown or deleted id with 422 "mcp_upstream_connection_not_found", and
the same connection twice with 422 "mcp_upstream_connection_duplicate".

To edit one row (enable, disable, rename, retitle) send the complete
upstreamMcpConnections array back via PUT: the array is preserved when
omitted, and PATCH reaches only /upstreamMcpConnections/{index}/alias.

_connectionId.description:
Connection of type `mcp` that holds the upstream server URL and
credentials. Each connection can be attached to a server once.

alias.description:
Short handle that namespaces the upstream's capabilities on this
server. Lowercased on save and unique per server (case-insensitive) —
a duplicate is rejected with 422 `mcp_upstream_duplicate_alias`, an
invalid character with 422 `mcp_upstream_invalid_alias_charset`.
Derived from the connection name when omitted on the first attach.

x-celigo-canon.reason: The charset and lowercase rules are enforced on POST and PUT; a PATCH of /upstreamMcpConnections/{index}/alias stores the value verbatim. The spec keeps the PUT-time rule so aliases stay valid on every write path.

name.description:
Current display name of the attached connection, joined from the
connection record on GET and list responses.

x-enumDescriptions.ok: The last discovery run fetched the upstream catalog successfully
x-enumDescriptions.failed: The last discovery run could not reach or parse the upstream server
x-enumDescriptions.never: Discovery has not run for this attachment yet

discoveryStatus.description:
Outcome of the most recent catalog discovery for this upstream. A new
attachment starts as `never`; a client-supplied value is ignored.

lastDiscoveredAt.description:
Timestamp when the upstream catalog was last discovered. Absent until
the first discovery run completes.

tools.description:
Upstream tools this server exposes. Only listed rows are served; a row
whose `upstreamName` disappears from the upstream catalog is kept and
flagged `unavailable`.

items.description:
One whitelisted upstream capability (tool or prompt). `upstreamName` is
the join key into the upstream catalog; the catalog-derived fields are
read-only and refreshed by discovery, while `overrides` changes how the
row is presented to MCP clients without touching the upstream definition.

_id.description:
Server-generated identifier for the row — the grant handle referenced
as `tool:<_id>` in resource grants and, for tool rows, accepted in
`permissionSets[]._toolIds`. Preserved across PUT while the row keeps
its `upstreamName`.

upstreamName.description:
Name of the capability as published by the upstream server. Must be
unique within the list — a repeat is rejected with 422
`mcp_upstream_duplicate_upstream_name`.

disabled.description:
When true, the row stays attached but is hidden from MCP clients and
does not count toward the server's enablement rule.

overrides.description:
Administrator-supplied presentation for an upstream row. Each field
replaces the discovered value MCP clients see; the upstream definition
itself is unchanged.

name.description:
Name exposed to MCP clients in place of `upstreamName`. The effective
name must be unique within the list — a collision with another row's
name is rejected with 422 `mcp_upstream_duplicate_effective_name`.

title.description: Display title exposed to MCP clients in place of the discovered title.

description.description: Description exposed to MCP clients in place of the discovered description.
examples: Ask a question about a public GitHub repository's codebase.

annotations.description:
MCP annotation hints merged over the discovered ones. Only the hints
you set are replaced; the rest keep their discovered value.

title.description: Human-readable title hint for the capability, displayed in MCP client UIs.

destructiveHint.description: Hints that the capability may delete or permanently modify data.

idempotentHint.description: Hints that repeated calls with the same input have no additional effect.

openWorldHint.description: Hints that the capability interacts with external systems whose results may vary between calls.

readOnlyHint.description: Hints that the capability only reads data and does not modify state.

changedSinceApproval.description:
When true, discovery found that the upstream definition differs from
the approved one. Cleared by the next PUT that includes
`upstreamMcpConnections`.

unavailable.description:
When true, the last discovery run no longer found this `upstreamName`
in the upstream catalog; the row is kept but not served and does not
count toward enablement.

discoveredAt.description: Timestamp when discovery last saw this capability in the upstream catalog.

title.description:
Display title shown to MCP clients — `overrides.title` when set,
otherwise the discovered title, otherwise `upstreamName`.

description.description:
Description shown to MCP clients — `overrides.description` when set,
otherwise the description discovered from the upstream catalog.
examples: Get a list of documentation topics for a GitHub repository.

name.description:
Name MCP clients see instead of `upstreamName`. Present only when
`overrides.name` is set.

prompts.description: Upstream prompts this server exposes, whitelisted by `upstreamName`.

resources.description: Upstream resources this server exposes, whitelisted by `upstreamName`.

uri.description:
Resource URI exposed to MCP clients via `resources/read`. Longer
values are rejected with 422 `mcp_upstream_resource_uri_max_size`.

_networkPolicyId.description:
Network policy whose IP allow and deny lists gate MCP protocol
requests to this server. Must reference a policy in the same
environment — any other id is rejected with 422 `invalid_ref`.
Preserved when omitted on PUT; send `null` (or PATCH `remove`) to
clear it, and deleting the policy with `?force=true` clears it too.
Absent from responses when no policy is assigned.

policies.description:
Traffic limits enforced on this server before a tool runs — a
server-level rate limit, a per-user rate limit, and a usage quota, each
optional and independent. At most one policy per `type` and
`keyResolver` is allowed; a second is rejected with 422
`mcp_server_duplicate_policy`. An empty array (the default) means
unlimited. Always returned; servers saved before traffic limits existed
return an empty array. Omitting the field on PUT clears every limit —
send the complete array back, or edit it with PATCH. A quota counts
calls accepted after it is saved; edits that keep the same `type` and
`keyResolver` keep counting from the original add time, and removing
the quota (then adding it again) starts a new count.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Leave `policies` empty unless the user asks for a limit — that is today's
default behavior. To change limits without touching the rest of the
document, PATCH `replace /policies` with the complete array.

items.description:
One traffic limit the server enforces before a tool runs — shown under
**Access > Governance** in the UI. A `rate-limit` caps calls per MINUTE,
HOUR, or DAY with a continuously refilling allowance, either for the whole
server (`keyResolver` `endpoint`) or separately for each OAuth end user
(`keyResolver` `consumer`); a `quota` caps cumulative calls over a UTC
calendar DAY, WEEK, or MONTH across every consumer. A call must pass every
enabled policy. A second policy of the same `type` and `keyResolver` is
rejected with 422 `mcp_server_duplicate_policy`. A rejected call is not
executed, does not count toward usage, and receives HTTP 429 with a
`Retry-After` header (seconds until the allowance refills or the quota
period resets), an `X-RateLimit-Limit` header, and a JSON-RPC error
(code -32004) whose message names the policy: `Rate limit exceeded: <name>`
or `Usage quota exceeded: <name>`. A quota counts only calls accepted after
it was added; editing the limit keeps the running count for the current UTC
period, and removing then re-adding the quota starts a new count.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Configure one policy per kind — one server-level rate limit, one per-user
rate limit (`keyResolver` `consumer`), one quota. A second policy of the
same `type` and `keyResolver` is rejected with 422
`mcp_server_duplicate_policy`.

A `tools/call` counts against every enabled policy, even when the named tool
does not exist; `initialize`, `tools/list`, `prompts/list`, and `resources/list`
are never counted or rejected (all live-verified). Whether `prompts/get` and
`resources/read` count has not been verified — do not assert either way.

Bearer API-token traffic is evaluated by `endpoint`-keyed rate limits and by
quotas only; a `consumer`-keyed rate limit applies to OAuth end users, each
with an independent allowance, and leaves API-token traffic untouched.

A rate limit keeps its allowance state when its `limit` is changed, so raising
a limit right after it tripped admits nothing until tokens refill at the new
rate. A quota counts calls accepted after it was added in the current UTC
period; editing the limit keeps the running count, and removing then
re-adding the quota starts a new count. Calls rejected by a traffic limit
do not consume quota, so raising a quota mid-period takes effect immediately.

x-enumDescriptions.rate-limit: Caps calls per MINUTE, HOUR, or DAY with an allowance that refills continuously; server-wide, or per end user with keyResolver consumer
x-enumDescriptions.quota: Caps cumulative calls over a UTC calendar DAY, WEEK, or MONTH for every consumer combined

type.description:
Kind of limit. Use rate-limit to protect downstream systems from bursts
and, with `keyResolver` `consumer`, to keep one end user from consuming
the whole server; use quota to cap total consumption for cost control.

name.description:
Required label for the limit, echoed verbatim in the 429 error message
that rejected clients receive — name it the way consumers should read
it. A missing or empty name is rejected with 422.

x-celigo-canon.reason: The Mongoose schema requires a non-empty name on save and the unit test `policy name is required` asserts a missing name is rejected at save time.

enabled.description:
When true, the policy is enforced. Set to false to keep the
configuration in place without enforcing it.

config.description:
Limit value and period. The maximum `limit` depends on the unit and
equals the platform ceiling of 300 calls per second over one period.

limit.description:
Maximum number of counted calls in one period. Ceilings per unit:
18000 per MINUTE, 1080000 per HOUR, 25920000 per DAY, 181440000 per
WEEK, 777600000 per MONTH — higher values are rejected with 422
`policy_config_invalid`.

x-celigo-canon.reason: The per-unit ceilings below are the server's own validation bounds, observed by probing one above and one at each ceiling for both rate limits and quotas.

periodTime.description:
Number of `periodTimeUnit` units in one period. Only a single unit
is supported; any other value is rejected with 422.

x-enumDescriptions.DAY: One calendar day (UTC) for quotas, or a one-day refilling allowance for rate limits

periodTimeUnit.description:
Length of one period. Rate limits take MINUTE, HOUR, or DAY; quotas
take DAY, WEEK, or MONTH — any other pairing, or a lowercase value,
is rejected with 422 `policy_config_invalid`.

x-enumDescriptions.endpoint: One shared allowance for the whole server across every consumer and authentication method
x-enumDescriptions.consumer: A separate allowance for each OAuth end user; bearer API-token traffic is not evaluated by this policy

oauth.description:
OAuth 2.0 configuration for the MCP server. Three modes are supported:

**Celigo-managed OAuth** — set `useCeligoOauth: true`. No issuer or
audience configuration needed; Celigo handles token validation.

**OAuth provider reference** — set `_mcpOAuthProviderId` to the ID of
a shared MCP OAuth provider resource (see `/v1/mcpoauthproviders`).
The provider holds the issuer, audience, and introspection settings.

**Inline custom OAuth** — set `issuerURL` and `audience` directly.
Tokens are validated against the issuer's JWKS. Optionally enable
`useIntrospection` for opaque tokens via RFC 7662.

Omit `oauth` entirely (or send `{}`) to disable OAuth on the server.
In responses, `oauth` is absent when no OAuth mode is configured.
The three modes are mutually exclusive. When using inline custom
OAuth, both `issuerURL` and `audience` are required. When
`useIntrospection` is `true`, `clientId` is also required.

x-celigo-canon.reason: The three-mode mutual exclusion stays a prose rule — a migration stratum of stored docs carries a provider reference alongside inline issuer fields, so a oneOf/not constraint would reject real responses.

useCeligoOauth.description:
When `true`, enables Celigo-managed OAuth. No external issuer
configuration is needed. Mutually exclusive with
`_mcpOAuthProviderId` and inline OAuth fields.

_mcpOAuthProviderId.description:
References a shared MCP OAuth provider resource that holds the
issuer, audience, scopes, and introspection settings. Mutually
exclusive with `useCeligoOauth` and inline OAuth fields.

Use `GET /v1/mcpoauthproviders` to list available providers.

issuerURL.description:
OAuth 2.0 issuer URL for inline custom OAuth.

Must be a well-formed URL with an explicit scheme — bare hostnames
and protocol-less values are rejected with 422 `invalid_uri`.
Use `https://` for production issuers.

audience.description:
Expected `aud` claim on incoming access tokens. Required when
using inline custom OAuth — omitting it returns
`missing_required_field` on `oauth.audience`.

useIntrospection.description:
When `true`, opaque access tokens are validated by calling the
issuer's RFC 7662 introspection endpoint using `clientId` /
`clientSecret`. When `false`, only JWT access tokens are accepted.

scopes.description:
Required OAuth scopes. Incoming tokens must carry every listed scope.

Rejected values return `enum` / `invalid_field_value` on
`oauth.scopes.<index>`.

x-enumDescriptions.mcp:read: Grants read-only access to MCP server resources.
x-enumDescriptions.mcp:write: Grants write access to MCP server resources.

clientId.description:
OAuth client ID used when introspecting opaque tokens. Required
when `useIntrospection` is `true`.

clientSecret.description:
OAuth client secret used with `clientId` for introspection. Masked
as `"******"` in response payloads; sending the masked value on
PUT is treated as "leave unchanged".
